title: A service issues a handle bound to a public key it names, for a person's agent
purpose: A broker handle is usable only with presentations signed by the holder key bound when it is issued (crates/lys-secrets/src/broker/admit.rs line 77). Today only the lys-secrets Issue command issues a handle, loading the holder key from a file (crates/lys-secrets/src/bin/lys-secrets/main.rs lines 136 to 146). So an agent started by Lys is launched with handle ids and no key that can present for them. ADR-125 gives each agent session one holder key, held by the runner in memory. This card gives the broker the route that issues a handle bound to that key's public key, asked for by lys-identity-server on behalf of the person who starts the agent.
task: Add POST /_lys/handles/issue. It admits only a screen service acting on behalf of a person, through the existing on-behalf admission. It issues a handle on a named secret to a named identity and a named Ed25519 public key through the broker's existing issue rules, and checks that the grant the lease counts against is rooted in the person acted for. It answers the handle id and token, and the issue is on the audit record as every issue is.

requirements.title: The issue route
requirements.spec: Behavioural. POST /_lys/handles/issue is a new route in crates/lys-secrets/src/bin/lys-secrets/serve.rs, handled in the new crates/lys-secrets/src/bin/lys-secrets/issue_route.rs. It admits a caller only through on_behalf (crates/lys-secrets/src/bin/lys-secrets/callers.rs line 104), which admits a screen service acting on behalf of a person. Any other caller is refused issue_service_only. The request is JSON holding identity, holder_key, secret, uses, not_after_ms and an optional spend_cap, and its type denies unknown members. The member holder_key is a 32-byte Ed25519 public key as 64 lower-case hex characters, and anything else is refused holder_key_invalid naming the length given. The route calls one new library function, Broker::issue_for_person in the new crates/lys-secrets/src/broker/issuing.rs. That function issues through issue_capped (crates/lys-secrets/src/broker.rs line 306) with a Holder of the identity and the key, so every rule issue_capped applies today still applies. It then checks that the person at the root of the grant (Permitted::person, crates/lys-secrets/src/permission.rs line 8) is the person acted for. If not, it refuses issue_person_mismatch naming both, and no handle is issued. The answer is the handle id and the handle token in hex, as the Issue command prints them (main.rs lines 160 and 161). The three refusals are one new enum IssueRefusal in crates/lys-secrets/src/error/issue.rs. SecretsError gains one variant Issue holding it by #[from], its name comes through error/name.rs, and refused in callers.rs (line 42) answers 400 for holder_key_invalid and 403 for the other two.
acceptance: A presentation signed by the named key is admitted for a handle the route issued, in crates/lys-secrets/tests/issue_route.rs.
A presentation signed by any other key is refused PresentationInvalid for that handle.
A caller without the screen service headers is refused issue_service_only.
A holder_key of 31 bytes is refused holder_key_invalid naming the length 31.
A request whose grant is rooted in a person other than the one acted for is refused issue_person_mismatch naming both.
After an issue_person_mismatch refusal the broker lists no new handle for that identity.
A request on a memory secret is refused MemoryNotUsable.
A request whose not_after_ms is at or before the broker's clock is refused InvalidLifetime.
A request holding a member outside those named is refused 400.

requirements.title: Every issue is on the audit record and its token in no log
requirements.spec: Behavioural. The route issues through issue_capped, which appends the issue's audit line of kind issue as it does for the Issue command, so the route adds no audit line of its own. A refused request appends nothing, as a refused issue does today. The handle token appears only in the route's answer. It is never written to a log line, an audit line or an error's words. The log-line test starts the broker with Served's start_logged (SECRETS-006 R2), which writes the broker's standard error to a file in the served root, and searches that file.
acceptance: One issue through the route appears once at GET /_lys/audit as a line of kind issue naming the identity and the secret.
A refused request adds no line to GET /_lys/audit.
No log line the broker writes during the test holds the handle token's hex.
No audit line holds the handle token's hex.

boundaries: SHALL NOT issue a handle to a key the broker made or holds. The holder key is only ever named by its public key.
SHALL NOT admit this route for a handle's own presentation or for a caller that is not a screen service acting on behalf of a person.
SHALL NOT change any rule issue_capped applies today.
SHALL NOT return, log or write a handle token anywhere but the route's answer.
SHALL NOT add a timeout, deadline, sleep, poll interval, #[allow], #[ignore] or any bypass.
SHALL NOT add a silent fallback. Every failure is a named refusal.
verification: The full Lys gate and ast-grep scan exit 0 at the card's head, measured by the card round.
`cargo test -p lys-secrets --test issue_route` exits 0 on Dean's laptop at the card's head.
